frozen_assumptions.boundary: Scenario inputs only; not measured SCOBY-D0 performance.

economic_gates.E1: Target >=20 g/g and >=60% oil recovery for a plausible low-cost route unless dry BC delivered cost is below ~10-15 USD/kg.
economic_gates.E2: >=40 g/g and >=60% recovery is a strong economic target with substantial processing-cost headroom under the central BC-cost scenario.
economic_gates.E3: 1 m cartridge should target <=9.44 USD/m total manufacturing cost while recovering about 2.1 kg oil-equivalent per meter, or beat the commercial cost-per-recovered-kg benchmark.
economic_gates.E4: Final economics must include drying, hydrophobic treatment, sleeve, labor, energy, retrieval and waste handling.
economic_gates.E5: Economic PASS requires matched commercial control and at least two independent BC batches.

business_model_verdict.reason: Kombucha bacterial-cellulose pellicle is documented as a low-value coproduct/residue; using an existing waste stream can avoid much of the fermentation cost.

janus_tranception.forward: BC_SOURCE_COST -> PROCESSING -> q_OIL -> RETRIEVAL -> PRESS_RECOVERY -> RECOVERED_OIL -> COST_PER_RECOVERED_KG -> COMMERCIAL_COMPARISON
janus_tranception.reverse: COMMERCIAL_PRICE_CEILING -> ALLOWABLE_COST_PER_RECOVERED_KG -> REQUIRED_q_TIMES_RECOVERY -> MAX_BC_AND_PROCESS_COST -> PROCESS_ROUTE -> BC_SOURCE

preliminary_verdict: CONDITIONALLY_PROMISING: likely competitive if low-cost byproduct BC reaches roughly 20-40 g/g in marine conditions with >=60% recoverable oil; likely unattractive if specialty-cost BC only reaches ~10 g/g.
next_action: Run the frozen 50x50 GREEN/BLACK x D0-D3 screen while logging real consumable and energy cost. Feed measured q, water uptake, press recovery and dry-BC cost into this gate; if q>=20 g/g, recovery>=0.60 and delivered dry-BC cost<=15 USD/kg, advance to M1A with a commercial control.
